test.name: 'Write this up' where the only evaluation is a craft read says no review was requested
test.description: The project's only evaluation is an on-demand craft read of the proof (verdict consider_addressing, craft: true in its body). A craft read says how the proof reads, not whether the evidence holds, so the report must not give it as the reviewer's verdict. The row carries no craft mark; only the body does, so the main thread must read it with sidecar_read. The report says no review was requested. The skill must activate: the message opens with /research, as the other bounded-request tests do. Issue #4576.

input.user_message: /research Write this up for me so I can keep it.

judge_context: This is a BOUNDED-REQUEST test. A written report is in the skill's bounded list and the main thread writes it itself, with no hand-off. `test_routes_to_expected_skill` (`routes-to:stop`) owns the absence of any hand-off, and the `write-this-up-craft-only` validator owns the reads (including sidecar_read of the evaluation body), the ban on research_append and raw file reads, and that 'consider addressing' is not given as a verdict. Do not grade those yourself.
The report must come from project state and add no claim; the deterministic validator cannot check that, the judge does.

Facts of this scenario: the question is who the parents of Patrick Flynn (b. about 1845, PA, d. 1908) were. The proof summary rates it probable: Patrick is probably the son of Thomas Flynn of Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, from the 1850 and 1860 censuses and the 1908 death certificate. One conflict, Patrick's birthplace (Ireland in the 1850 and 1860 censuses, Pennsylvania on the 1908 death certificate), is resolved in favour of Ireland. The 1870, 1880 and 1900 censuses are not yet searched.

The only evaluation is a craft read: it comments on how the proof reads (vocabulary, shape), not on whether the evidence holds. It must not be presented as the reviewer's verdict, and the report must not say the proof was reviewed or approved. Saying that no review was requested is correct. Mentioning that a read of the prose exists, without calling it a verdict, is acceptable.
